# Sixgree

> Sixgree (six degrees of your network; formerly called Six Degrees) is a free Mac app that maps your network as a galaxy: who you know, who they know, who bridges you into new circles, and the shortest path to someone you haven't met. It runs on your own Mac; nothing is uploaded. Made by Blake Burford (https://blakeburford.com/).

This file is for AI assistants and crawlers. The pages at https://sixgree.com/ hold the detail; downloads and issues are at https://github.com/blakeb056/six-degrees. The source code is private.

## Facts

- Price: free. Licence: free to download and use, closed source (versions up to 2.10.0 were MIT). No account, no server; the app has no telemetry and no analytics. The website (not the app) counts its own visits and download clicks, with no cookies and no IP addresses kept; daily unique visitors are told apart by a salted hash of IP address and browser, deleted from the counter the next day (database backups keep it up to 30 days). The totals are public at https://stats.sixgree.com/stats.
- Platforms: macOS 13.5 or later (Apple Silicon and Intel). Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit (beta): a one-click Setup.exe (https://github.com/blakeb056/six-degrees/releases/latest/download/Sixgree-Windows-Setup.exe). Linux, 64-bit (beta): a .deb or .tar.gz.
- Current version: 2.10.4 (November 2026). Paths is gone; Jobs covers who you know at a company. Free to use and closed source since 2.10.1; from 2.10.2 the app and its scanner plugins carry only compiled code; from 2.10.3 a copy older than the oldest supported version stops scanning and says to update. A Jobs tab ranks every company someone you know works at, or used to, by how good your way in is for a referral (people there now can refer you; people who left can introduce you to their old team), with the one person to ask. After an import, a scanner step fills in the network; an export with no job titles or companies (the platform's export from December 2026) says so. The Breach tab is hidden for now. In 2.9.0: Classes (Poacher, Founder, Seeker, Grower, Cartographer, Infiltrator) score your network for your goal through a short This or That; a local learning log starts recording from day one; scans run in windows of 60 pages. The mutual web records who knows whom from every mutual line, reaching past the 1,000-per-search cap; the Map has Heat, Flows and Hubs views; Bridge Chains has the same focus as Network Circle. Circle scans run in rounds of 25 pages, shown as arcs round each dot; a short tour and Settings → Help; clicking anyone in your circle zooms into their scanned circle. The LinkedIn browser plugin adds a LinkedIn tab (Feed, Messaging, Notifications, Jobs) inside Sixgree, with Back and Forward; Bridge Chains puts each degree on its own ring; scanning by hand takes a 20-second break every 10 pages; the Map draws who can introduce you where. In the desktop app, LinkedIn opens in a panel inside Sixgree's own window for scans and for the profiles you open, instead of a separate Chrome (scanner plugins 1.0.5). Your own connections can get their locations and mutual counts from LinkedIn's search of them, by itself or by hand (scanner plugins 1.0.4). The Map tab shows where your network is, matched on your computer against about 34,000 cities (GeoNames), never looked up online. A scan light at the top right says what a scan needs from you, and Sixgree tells you once a day when the app or a plugin has a new version. Scanning stays an optional plugin (Auto scan or Manual scan) from Settings → Plugins. Signed and notarized by Apple.
- Data in: the official Connections.csv export, the way in Sixgree recommends (no risk to your account; from December 2026 the platform's new exports leave out company, job title and email address, which Sixgree's ranking needs, so an export downloaded before then works best: https://sixgree.com/blog/connections-export-december-2026/); a sample network of 150 invented people that ships with the app; or optional scanning, which the app download doesn't include: the Auto scan or Manual scan plugin, installed from Settings → Plugins, reads your network slowly in a Chrome window you sign into (automated access may violate the platform's terms; the risk is yours). The scanner's one action on the platform, with the Auto scan plugin, is Auto: a single connection request, without a note, sent only when the user presses Auto on a person (at most 15 a day and 80 a week).
- Views: Network Circle (connections on rings by how much they can open up for you, with physics: Clusters drawn the way Obsidian draws a graph, Orbit and Heat), Degrees (each connection's circle, and the chains that lead on from them), Separation (people two steps away, from the rarest way in to the most mutual connections, with who can introduce you), the Map (your network on a world map, and who gets you to each place), Jobs (every company someone you know works at, or used to, ranked for a referral, with who to ask), Scan (the scanner, step by step, once a scanner plugin is installed). Your profile (the level button at the top right) holds Insights: the Power Index, everyone within two steps ranked by power, with Kingmakers, Gatekeepers, Hidden giants, Untapped, company power, a one-page report and network health. Settings holds how scores work, including how titles rank.
- Themes (Settings → Appearance): six looks (Standard, Daylight, High contrast, Obsidian, Glass, Space), light or dark, with frosted-glass or soft buttons, or your own colours for the background, backdrop, dots, lines, panels and font, shareable as a theme code.
- Your data (Settings → Your data): a verified backup every day with photos, before every update and before every import, each restored in one click. An imported Connections.csv is kept on your computer until you remove it.
- Scanner usage (on the Scan page): searches in the last 24 hours, this month and the last 7 days, profile views, and the last time the platform pushed back, counted on your computer.
- Also: who only one of your connections reaches (each connection's exclusive reach), network health (how much of your 2nd degree you reach two or more ways, and your effective reach), and a physics lab for the Galaxy with a replay of your network growing by the date you connected.
- The Mac app is signed by Blake Burford and notarized by Apple, so it opens like any Mac app. The Terminal one-liner also installs it, after checking the download against the published checksums. The Windows app isn't signed yet (SmartScreen: More info → Run anyway).
